findings.summary: GetFlagCompletionFunc and FixedCompletions now return the named type CompletionFunc instead of the unnamed func type, so code that uses reflection to compare types or uses the result as a type parameter could behave differently (edge case).

judge.reason: Talks about reflection/type parameter edge cases, not the compile-time assignability break for user-defined named func types.

votes.label: false_alarm
votes.reason: Talks about reflection/type parameter edge cases, not the compile-time assignability break for user-defined named func types.

votes.label: valid_other
votes.reason: Describes the reflection/type-name effect of the new named type, matching the known 'other real problem', not the compile-breaking assignability bug.

votes.label: valid_other
votes.reason: Reflection/type-identity change is the known other problem; it doesn't identify the compile break for user-defined named func types.

votes.label: valid_other
votes.reason: Points to reflection/type-identity differences from the new named type, which matches the known reflection issue, but it does not describe the compile break when a user's named func type is passed to ValidArgsFunction or RegisterFlagCompletionFunc.
